data.description:
Specialized Manufacturers Draw Investor Interest Across the U.S. Metals Industry

Specialized Manufacturers Draw Investor Interest Across the U.S. Metals Industry

PR Newswire

CHICAGO, Nov. 19, 2026

BGL Metals & Advanced Metals Manufacturing Insider

CHICAGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The U.S. Metals industry has entered a favorable period for investment and consolidation, according to an industry report released by the Metals & Advanced Metals Manufacturing investment banking team at Brown Gibbons Lang & Company (BGL). Strong opportunities exist across the fragmented U.S. service center, advanced metals manufacturing, and other metal-related markets to build scaled platforms around specialized capabilities and scarce production capacity.

 BGL examines key forces reshaping the U.S. metals industry and the growing investment and M&A opportunities.

Download and read the BGL Metals & Advanced Metals Manufacturing Insider here: https://bit.ly/BGLMetalsInsiderNovember2026

BGL Managing Director Vince Pappalardo: "Some of the most attractive investment opportunities are in the downstream manufacturers that turn metal into specialized components. These businesses often have capabilities, customer qualifications, and production capacity that are difficult to replicate, making them increasingly important to strategic buyers and private equity investors."

BGL Director Hubert de la Vauvre: "We are seeing improvement directly in the deal environment. There has been an uptick in pitching activity, particularly for healthy manufacturers with strong backlogs and exposure to faster-growing end markets."

Inside the report, BGL examines key forces reshaping the U.S. metals industry and the growing investment and M&A opportunities across the value chain.

Key takeaways:

  • The market forces creating favorable conditions for investment and consolidation across the U.S. metals industry
  • Where the investment opportunity is growing across the metals value chain
  • The notable transactions that signal growing investor participation in selected metals end-markets

BGL expects Metals M&A activity to remain strong into 2027. The combination of domestic investment, growing end-market demand, and continued fragmentation is creating opportunities for both strategic acquirers and private equity firms.

About BGL's Metals & Advanced Metals Manufacturing Investment Banking Team

BGL's Metals & Advanced Metals Manufacturing team has deep sector knowledge and extensive Metals M&A transaction experience within major subsectors of the broader metals industry. Coverage includes mills and foundries, metals recycling, advanced metals manufacturing, and metal service centers.

About Brown Gibbons Lang & Company
Brown Gibbons Lang & Company (BGL) is a leading independent investment bank and financial advisory firm focused on the global middle market. The firm advises private and public corporations and private equity groups on mergers and acquisitions, capital markets, financial restructurings, business valuations and opinions, and other strategic matters. BGL has offices in Boston, Chicago, Cleveland, Los Angeles, and New York. The firm is also a founding member of REACH Cross-Border Mergers & Acquisitions, enabling BGL to service clients in 30 countries around the world. Securities transactions are conducted through Brown, Gibbons, Lang & Company Securities, LLC, an affiliate of Brown Gibbons Lang & Company LLC and a registered broker-dealer and member of FINRA and SIPC. data.title: AM Best Revises Outlooks to Positive for United National Life Insurance Company of America
data.description:
AM Best Revises Outlooks to Positive for United National Life Insurance Company of America

AM Best has revised the outlooks to positive from stable and affirmed the Financial Strength Rating of B++ (Good) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating of “bbb+” (Good) of United National Life Insurance Company of America (UNL) (Omaha, NE).

The Credit Ratings (ratings) reflect UNL’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its adequate operating performance, limited business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM).

The positive outlook reflects the trend of favorable operating performance UNL has exhibited to date. The company has reported consistent premium growth. Additionally, UNL’s operating return-on-revenue (ROR) and return-on-equity (ROE) metrics have been maintained in the high double digit range with the five-year ROR and ROE at 23.1% and 24.7%, respectively.

UNL’s balance sheet strength is very strong, supported by capital growth through retained earnings and modest dividends. UNL’s business profile is limited with its core supplemental health and final expense products geared mostly to the over-65 senior market. UNL has a formal ERM program that is mature with established processes and a good governance structure.

This press release relates to Credit Ratings that have been published on AM Best’s website. For all rating information relating to the release and pertinent disclosures, including details of the office responsible for issuing each of the individual ratings referenced in this release, please see AM Best’s Recent Rating Activity web page. data.title: Vail Resorts Turns Up the Volume with ILLENIUM in Vail, John Summit in Whistler and a Full Winter of Music and Mountain Culture
data.description:
Vail Resorts Turns Up the Volume with ILLENIUM in Vail, John Summit in Whistler and a Full Winter of Music and Mountain Culture

Vail Resorts Turns Up the Volume with ILLENIUM in Vail, John Summit in Whistler and a Full Winter of Music and Mountain Culture

PR Newswire

BROOMFIELD, Colo., Nov. 19, 2026
  • ILLENIUM opens Vail Mountain's biggest music season to date on Dec. 11, 2026, and John Summit returns to Whistler Blackcomb on March 20-21, 2027
  • Guests who want a front-row seat to music and culture in the mountains should lock in an Epic Pass; Last chance to buy a Pass is December 6

Images Approved for Media Use Available HERE

BROOMFIELD, Colo., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Vail Resorts is turning up the volume this winter. GRAMMY-nominated producer ILLENIUM opens Vail Mountain's biggest music season to date on Dec. 11, 2026, and John Summit returns to Whistler Blackcomb on March 20-21, 2027, headlining a season of live music, après and mountain culture across the company's resorts. Additional headline performances will be announced as the season gets underway.

From on-mountain DJ sets to village celebrations, intimate dinners and milestone anniversaries, resorts including Vail Mountain, Breckenridge, Whistler Blackcomb, Park City Mountain, Beaver Creek Resort, Keystone Resort, and Heavenly Mountain Resort will host new events and returning favorites that immerse guests in music and mountain culture. Vail Mountain leads the way with seven on-mountain pop-up performances – three more than last season – plus two new on-mountain music venues. Guests who want a front-row seat to the season should lock in an Epic Pass; last chance to buy a Pass is December 6.

"Music and après culture have always been part of our mountain experience," said Jody Churich, Senior Vice President of Destination Resorts at Vail Resorts. "From ILLENIUM in Vail and John Summit in Whistler to village performances and dance parties, these are experiences people will remember long after the lifts stop spinning. This winter, we're bringing even more of them to resorts across our mountain portfolio."

Music Across the Mountains

Headline Performances: From GRAMMY-nominated headliners in Vail to a house music takeover in Whistler, the season's biggest names bring festival energy to the mountains.

  • At Vail Mountain (CO), GRAMMY-nominated, multi-platinum recording artists ILLENIUM opens the 2026/27 music season Dec. 11 at the newly renovated Dobson Arena in Lionshead. Ian Asher follows Jan. 16, with tickets available at AXS.com. Another headliner will be announced for an April 10 show at Dobson.
  • At Whistler Blackcomb (BC), John Summit's Experts Only returns to Lot 7 March 20–21 after making its Whistler debut last March. More lineup details are coming soon, and tickets are available HERE.
  • At Heavenly (CA/NV), Elderbrook headlines the Season Kickoff party Dec. 19 at Lakeview Lodge, high above Lake Tahoe, setting the tone for a winter of DJ performances.
  • At Park City Mountain (UT), the energy of Shaun White's The Snow League spills over from the superpipe to Eagle Plaza in Mountain Village where LP Giobbi performs Jan. 22 and Dombresky brings Disco Dom on Jan. 23. Both shows are free and open to the public.

Après and Live Music: From DJ sets at the base of Vail Mountain's Gondola One to mountaintop music sessions on Whistler Mountain, guests will find new and returning ways to keep the energy going on mountain and after the lifts stop spinning.

  • At Vail Mountain (CO), this is the biggest music season yet, with seven on-mountain performances (three more than last winter) and two new music venues. Vail Après Club™ builds on a 2025/26 season that brought globally recognized artists including Sofi Tukker, Dillon Francis, Chris Lorenzo and John Summit to the mountain. This season, new artists, venues and mountain activations will be announced on social media @VailMtn. Every Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 2:30 to 5:30 p.m., Après All Day at Vail Express Lift Bar brings more than 50 performing artists to the stage, nearly double than last season, in collaboration with Vail Mountain partner Outer Range Brewing Co. Next to the Legendary Back Bowls Gate, the reimagined Vail Ice Bar blends alpine nostalgia with a lively outdoor gathering space for drinks, music and après in the heart of the mountain.
  • At Breckenridge (CO), the Kingdom of Breck™ comes to life with high-energy live music across the mountain and in town. The excitement begins during the Rockstar Energy Open with free performances by RL Grime and PHRVA at Blue River Plaza. Throughout the season, and perched high on Peak 9, The Overlook becomes an après destination for the Après at the Overlook Music Series, with live DJ sets and drink specials set against 11,000-foot views. Nearby, Keystone (CO) brings back Keystone After Dark, inviting guests to keep après going into the evening near the largest mountaintop snow structure in North America on six select dates.
  • At Whistler Blackcomb (BC), the village après scene is as much a part of the trip as the alpine. Whistler favorites including the Hairfarmers and Taylor James will play at Merlin's, GLC and Dusty's all season long. Up top, the popular Corona DJ Sessions return to the Corona Mountain Top Lodge on Whistler Mountain starting Jan. 17, with more details coming soon.
  • At Park City Mountain (UT), Canyons Village is the place to be when the lifts stop spinning. Après at the Airstream DJ sets keep the energy going at the Umbrella Bar every Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 2 to 5 p.m. starting Nov. 27. Canyons Village Silver Sky Nights pair live music with fireworks over the village on Dec. 18, Jan. 16, Feb. 6 and Feb. 13.
  • At Heavenly (CA/NV), après comes with a view of Lake Tahoe. The Views and Vibes series brings popular DJs including Elderbrook, Bob Moses, Vandelux and Snakehips to the stage high above the lake all season long.
  • At Mount Snow (VT), the après traditions run deep and the parties run late. Snow Barn, a rite of passage for any Mount Snow visit, brings live music, DJs and late-night entertainment starting Dec. 19, with acts including One More Time, Lazer Dad and Haus of Monsters. Local favorite Bruce Jacques returns to Cuzzins for another season of sing-along performances, and reservations go fast. On Jan. 30, the Carinthia Lodge House Party fills all three floors of the lodge with music, drinks and games. In spring, Reggaefest brings live reggae from IRIEspect to the main stage March 20–22.

"There's an energy in a mountain town when the music starts, and at many of our resorts you'll hear it from the slopes all the way into town," said Churich. "It might be a band on a sunny mountaintop deck or a headliner on a village stage after the lifts stop. Whether guests are front row for the big show or dancing in ski boots with friends after a day on the snow, we want every one of them to leave with a story and an unforgettable moment."

Epic Pass Holders Get More Out of Every Event; Last chance to buy a Pass is December 6
Last chance to buy an Epic Pass is Dec. 6, so guests eager to get on the mountain this winter still have time to lock in access and savings. With new savings for young adults, guests ages 13–30 save 20% on an Epic Pass or Epic Local Pass. Plus, all guests who purchase an Epic Pass or Epic Local Pass now will receive five Epic Friend Tickets offering 50% off adult lift tickets, making it easier to bring the crew along and save. Epic Pass Holders can also save on the rest of their trip with exclusive savings through Epic Mountain Rewards, including 20% off food, lodging, lessons, rentals, and more.

About Vail Resorts, Inc.
Vail Resorts operates a network of 42 iconic mountain resorts across North America, Europe, and Australia. Our portfolio includes premier destinations such as Vail Mountain, Beaver Creek, Breckenridge, Park City Mountain, Whistler Blackcomb, and Keystone; beloved regional mountains like Stowe, Heavenly, and Northstar; and local resorts close to metro areas that help to introduce the next generation of skiers and riders to the sport. Together, these resorts provide guests with an unmatched range of mountain experiences connected through the Epic Pass. We are passionate about providing an Experience of a Lifetime to our team members and guests. Through our environmental and social responsibility work, we are committed to reaching a zero net operating footprint by 2030, supporting our employees and communities, and broadening engagement in our sport. Beyond our resorts, Vail Resorts operates industry-leading ski and ride school programs, rental operations, distinctive dining and hospitality experiences, retail operations, and the Grand Teton Lodge Company. Learn more about our company at www.VailResorts.com, or discover our resorts and Pass options at www.EpicPass.com.

data.title: Mile High Labs Files Type II Drug Master File with FDA for CBD Isolate
data.description:
Mile High Labs Files Type II Drug Master File with FDA for CBD Isolate

Mile High Labs Files Type II Drug Master File with FDA for CBD Isolate

PR Newswire

LOVELAND, Colo., Nov. 19, 2026

Mile High Labs continues to build its pharmaceutical-channel capabilities with a Type II DMF for CBD Isolate

LOVELAND, Colo., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mile High Labs, a global leader in hemp-derived cannabinoid ingredients, today announced that it has filed a Type II Drug Master File (DMF #044151) with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for its CBD Isolate, a 98% cannabidiol isolate. The file was submitted on October 2, 2026.

Companies developing drug products can reference DMF #044151 in their own FDA submissions through a Letter of Authorization from Mile High Labs.

"This filing reflects how we have always run this business," said John Davis, Chief Operating Officer of Mile High Labs. "As our industry has matured over the past decade, investing in quality has remained our true north at Mile High Labs, enabling us to bring our cannabinoid ingredients into highly regulated markets around the world. Our Type II Drug Master File for CBD Isolate represents an important milestone in our ongoing advancement within the pharmaceutical channel, building on a unified quality system that already supplies consumer and regulated medicinal products. As we continue to expand our pharmaceutical capabilities and regulatory readiness, we're excited to be preparing for an FDA inspection and strengthening our ability to serve drug developers in the U.S. and abroad."

The file is expected to appear on FDA's public list of Drug Master Files in its next quarterly update.

About Mile High Labs

For over 10 years, Mile High Labs has been committed to high-quality hemp-derived cannabinoid ingredients, supplying brands and formulators in the United States, United Kingdom, European Union, Japan and other regulated markets. Based in Loveland, Colorado, the company's portfolio includes CBD, CBG, CBN and CBC isolates, distillates and water-soluble formats.

data.title: Why Micron, Broadcom and other AI stocks have given up their gains
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

The Anthropic enthusiasm has faded while China concerns have intensified

Micron's stock has turned lower for the day.

For a period of time on Thursday, it looked like the excitement over Anthropic's initial public offering would give artificial-intelligence stocks a much-awaited boost. Now the trading action is decidedly more mixed.

Shares of companies like Nvidia (NVDA), Micron Technology (MU) and Broadcom (AVGO) that had been riding a broad-based AI rally this morning have since surrendered their gains and turned lower. Some of the AI stocks still in positive territory on Thursday, including Intel (INTC) and Coherent (COHR), have their own specific catalysts.

Part of the issue may be that Anthropic's IPO prompted investors to shift up their holdings, according to Iskandar Rakhmatov, a portfolio manager at quantitative-strategy research platform Zeus Quanto.

"Investors who wanted the purest AI exposure got it today, and some of them sold Nvidia and other chip names to fund the new position," he told MarketWatch.

Granted, the excitement around Anthropic itself has also waned. Shares (ANT) opened 34% higher midday Thursday, but they've since pared gains to be up just 15% from their IPO price of $83.

Jack Amy, a quantitative-trading analyst at European digital wealth platform Moneyfarm, noted that at first, the Anthropic IPO "gave broader U.S. equities a lift, helping to steady nerves after a choppy week for tech."

"However, those wider gains have since pared back as macro concerns, specifically around tightening financial conditions and what that means for the capital-intensive AI trade, continue to weigh on sentiment," he added in emailed comments.

There are also renewed jitters about export policies after a report from a short seller discussed whether Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) chips have made it into Chinese servers. AMD didn't respond to a MarketWatch request for comment.

"The China issues are likely to permeate across the semi industry as export controls are tightened," said Michael Casper, senior market strategist at wealth-management firm HB Wealth.

Investors have generally been worried that the U.S. government would take a tougher tack on sales of advanced technology to China in light of recent turmoil involving Nvidia.

See also: Jensen Huang was a 'China salesman' for Nvidia. His exit is weighing on Chinese tech stocks.

Heading into Thursday's trading day, D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria told MarketWatch that Anthropic's IPO was "pivotal" for the AI investment cycle.

Luria said that a successful IPO could "extend the cycle by years," while an unsuccessful one could "stall investment" into the ecosystem.

See also: Can Anthropic's IPO do for the stock market what Nvidia's earnings couldn't?

Morningstar analyst Martin Szumski doubted the IPO would "fully turn around what has been very bearish sentiment lately." One reason is that investors saw Anthropic's prospectus weeks ago and knew "relatively what to expect."

The AI stocks that managed to hold onto some gains on Thursday have some idiosyncratic drivers. Shares of Coherent were up 1.4% after the optical company announced a new buyback program, while shares of Intel were up 2.7% following reports of remarks from a conference indicating that the company locked in an outside customer for its 18A manufacturing technology.

CoreWeave's stock, meanwhile, gave up a double-digit percentage gain and was recently off 5%, despite a co-founder's disclosure that he purchased $30 million of the company's bruised bonds with the intention to hold them until maturity in 2031.

Don't miss: A CoreWeave co-founder just made an unconventional $30 million wager on its battered bonds

-Hannah Pedone

data.title: Mindgruve Appoints Former WPP Executive Steve Terjeson as Vice President of Technology
data.description:
Mindgruve Appoints Former WPP Executive Steve Terjeson as Vice President of Technology

Mindgruve Appoints Former WPP Executive Steve Terjeson as Vice President of Technology

PR Newswire

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 19, 2026

Former Choreograph technology leader to accelerate AI innovation, advance Mindgruve's proprietary Sightline platform, and scale enterprise technology capabilities.

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mindgruve, a modern media, commerce, and data technology company, today announced the appointment of Steve Terjeson as Vice President of Technology. Terjeson will lead Mindgruve's software development and data engineering teams, advancing the agency's established technology capabilities while accelerating innovation, scalability, and enterprise integration. A key priority will be driving the next generation of Sightline, Mindgruve's proprietary predictive marketing and business intelligence platform.

"Technology and data intelligence have long been central to how Mindgruve delivers measurable business growth for our clients," said Chad Robley, CEO of Mindgruve. "Sightline gives us a differentiated advantage that even the largest holding companies are working to replicate. Steve brings the enterprise technology experience to accelerate that advantage, scale our innovation, and deliver the sophistication of a global holding company with the agility and speed of an independent agency."

Terjeson joins Mindgruve from WPP's Choreograph, where he served as Vice President and acting CTO of data and technology for North America. He led enterprise data and technology delivery for global brands, managed a globally distributed engineering team, and developed sophisticated cloud data systems connecting brands' data to leading platforms, including Google and Adobe. He previously held senior roles at Wunderman Thompson (WPP), The Richards Group, and Costco Travel, with client experience spanning IBM, Uber, The Home Depot, and NBCUniversal.

"I've worked with marketing technology at nearly every scale throughout my career, and what Mindgruve has built stands alongside the very best," said Steve Terjeson, Vice President of Technology at Mindgruve. "The opportunity to build on an already sophisticated technology ecosystem, accelerate Sightline's evolution, and bring even more powerful AI and data-driven solutions to global brands is incredibly compelling. Mindgruve has the technology, talent, and entrepreneurial culture to move faster and deliver greater impact for clients."

In his new role, Terjeson will oversee Mindgruve's technology strategy and roadmap, with a focus on expanding the agency's AI, software engineering, cloud infrastructure, and data integration capabilities. He will also help accelerate the evolution of Sightline, strengthening its predictive intelligence, enterprise scalability, and ability to connect marketing investments directly to business outcomes. His leadership will further enhance the agency's commitment to delivering secure, flexible, and enterprise-grade technology solutions that enable smarter decisions, stronger marketing performance, and more profitable growth.

To learn how Mindgruve can turn your data into measurable growth, visit mindgruve.com/contact.

About Mindgruve
Mindgruve is a modern media, commerce, and data technology company comprised of strategists, creatives, media and commerce experts, data scientists, and engineers driven by one common purpose — accelerate business growth for our brand partners through data-driven marketing. With over 750 experts worldwide, Mindgruve's teams deliver integrated media and commerce solutions for global brands.

data.title: U.S. Treasury 10-Year TIPS Auction Pays Highest Yield in 24 Years
data.description:
By Paulo Trevisani

A U.S. Treasury auction of 10-year inflation-protected securities on Thursday cleared the highest yield in 24 years.

The Treasury sold $19 billion in 10-year TIPS paying a high yield of 2.903%, the highest since July 2002, when the high yield was 3.099%.

Thursday's auction was a reopening, while the one in July 2002 was a new issue.

The bid-to-cover ratio, a measure of demand for the securities, increased to 2.43 from 2.24 in the latest 10-year TIPS auction, held in September.

Indirect bidders, a group that includes foreign buyers, took $12.97 billion in competitive bids.

The auction happened as sticky inflation increased the chances of a steep rise in interest rates by the Federal Reserve.
